# Docs

- Python Notes
  - [Python Learning Notes](/en/docs): Phase-by-phase Python notes, written for a JavaScript/TypeScript developer
  - Phase 1 — Core Foundations
    - [Phase 1 — Python Core Foundations](/en/docs/phase-1): Goals for this phase, and a full JS/TS → Python cheat sheet
    - [Syntax & Indentation](/en/docs/phase-1/syntax-and-indentation): Python's biggest rule coming from JS/TS — indentation defines blocks
    - [Variables & Constants](/en/docs/phase-1/variables-and-constants): No const, let, or var — Python just assigns
    - [Data Types & None](/en/docs/phase-1/data-types-and-none): str, int, float, bool, None, and checking types with type()
    - [Printing & String Interpolation](/en/docs/phase-1/printing-and-strings): print() instead of console.log(), and f-strings instead of template literals
    - [Operators](/en/docs/phase-1/operators): Arithmetic, comparison, and logical operators — and, or, not instead of &&, ||, !
    - [if / elif / else](/en/docs/phase-1/conditionals): Conditionals, including nested conditions
    - [for, range() & while](/en/docs/phase-1/loops): Looping in Python — one of the bigger syntax changes from JS/TS
    - [break, continue & pass](/en/docs/phase-1/loop-control): Controlling loops, plus Python's "do nothing yet" keyword
  - Phase 2 — Collections
    - [Phase 2 — Collections](/en/docs/phase-2): Goals for this phase, and a full JS/TS → Python cheat sheet
    - [list, Indexing & Slicing](/en/docs/phase-2/lists): Python's array — ordered, mutable, and allows duplicates
    - [append, remove & pop](/en/docs/phase-2/list-methods): The three list methods you'll use constantly
    - [tuple](/en/docs/phase-2/tuples): A list that can't be changed after it's created
    - [set](/en/docs/phase-2/sets): A collection that automatically removes duplicates
    - [dict](/en/docs/phase-2/dictionaries): Python's object — probably the most important type for backend work
    - [get, keys, values & items](/en/docs/phase-2/dictionary-methods): The methods you'll use to safely read and loop over a dict
    - [Nested Data & in](/en/docs/phase-2/nested-data-and-in): A list of dicts (very common in backend code), and Python's membership operator
  - Phase 3 — Functions
    - [Phase 3 — Functions](/en/docs/phase-3): Goals for this phase, and a full JS/TS → Python cheat sheet
    - [Defining Functions](/en/docs/phase-3/functions-basics): def instead of function, parameters, and return
    - [Type Hints](/en/docs/phase-3/type-hints): The Python equivalent of TypeScript's parameter and return types
    - [Default & Keyword Arguments](/en/docs/phase-3/default-and-keyword-arguments): Optional parameters, and calling functions by argument name
    - [*args & **kwargs](/en/docs/phase-3/args-and-kwargs): Accepting any number of positional or keyword arguments
  - Phase 4 — Python OOP
    - [Phase 4 — Python OOP](/en/docs/phase-4): Goals for this phase, and a full TypeScript → Python cheat sheet
    - [class & object](/en/docs/phase-4/classes-and-objects): Defining a class, and creating an object from it — no new keyword
    - [__init__ & self](/en/docs/phase-4/init-and-self): Python's constructor, and the explicit stand-in for this
    - [Methods](/en/docs/phase-4/methods): Functions that belong to a class — and why self still shows up
    - [Inheritance & super()](/en/docs/phase-4/inheritance): extends becomes parentheses, and super() works almost the same
  - Phase 5 — Python-specific Features
    - [Phase 5 — Python-specific Features](/en/docs/phase-5): Goals for this phase, and a full JS/TS → Python cheat sheet
    - [List Comprehension](/en/docs/phase-5/list-comprehension): A one-line way to build a list — Python's version of .map() and .filter()
    - [Dictionary Comprehension](/en/docs/phase-5/dictionary-comprehension): The same idea as list comprehension, but building a dict
    - [enumerate](/en/docs/phase-5/enumerate): Loop over a list while also getting the index
    - [zip](/en/docs/phase-5/zip): Loop over two lists together, pair by pair
  - Phase 6 — Exceptions + Modules
    - [Phase 6 — Exceptions + Modules](/en/docs/phase-6): Goals for this phase, and a full JS/TS → Python cheat sheet
    - [try / except](/en/docs/phase-6/try-except): Python's try/catch — but it wants you to name the specific error
    - [raise](/en/docs/phase-6/raise): Python's throw — with built-in exception types instead of a generic Error
    - [Modules & Imports](/en/docs/phase-6/modules-and-imports): How Python files talk to each other — no export keyword needed
  - Phase 7 — Type Hints
    - [Phase 7 — Type Hints](/en/docs/phase-7): Goals for this phase, and a full TypeScript → Python cheat sheet
    - [Variable & Function Hints](/en/docs/phase-7/variable-and-function-hints): Annotating plain values, and a recap of function type hints
    - [Container Hints](/en/docs/phase-7/container-hints): Describing what's inside a list or dict, not just that it is one
    - [Optional & Nested Types](/en/docs/phase-7/optional-and-nested): A value that might be None, and combining container hints together
  - Phase 8 — async / await
    - [Phase 8 — async / await](/en/docs/phase-8): Goals for this phase, and a JS/TS → Python cheat sheet
    - [def, async def & await](/en/docs/phase-8/async-and-await): Same idea as JS async/await — almost the same keywords too
  - [Final Practice — Build a User Store](/en/docs/final-practice): Close the tutorial and build this yourself — the best prep for FastAPI
- Backend with FastAPI
  - [Backend Development with FastAPI](/en/docs/fastapi): A syllabus for teaching backend development with FastAPI
  - Web Fundamentals
    - [What is the Internet?](/en/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/what-is-the-internet): The network that makes backend development possible
    - [What is a Website?](/en/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/what-is-a-website): HTML, CSS, and JS — and what actually happens when a page loads
    - [Web 1.0, Web 2.0 & Why React](/en/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/web-evolution-and-why-react): The full page reload problem — and why modern apps stopped doing it
    - [What is the Backend, and Why Do We Need One?](/en/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/why-we-need-a-backend): Why business logic can't just live in the browser
    - [What is a Database?](/en/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/what-is-a-database): Where the backend keeps data that has to survive and stay organized
    - [Putting It Together — How Does YouTube Work?](/en/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/how-youtube-works): A real-world walkthrough that ties client, backend, database, and file storage together
  - Getting Started
    - [What is FastAPI?](/en/docs/fastapi/getting-started/what-is-fastapi): A modern Python framework built for writing APIs fast, with less code
    - [Project Setup](/en/docs/fastapi/getting-started/project-setup): Virtual environments, and installing FastAPI's core dependencies
    - [Environment Configuration](/en/docs/fastapi/getting-started/environment-configuration): Keeping database credentials out of your code with a .env file
    - [Database Connection](/en/docs/fastapi/getting-started/database-connection): Turning your connection string into a real connection with SQLAlchemy
  - Building the Todo API
    - [Creating the Todo Model](/en/docs/fastapi/todo-api/creating-the-todo-model): Describing a database table as a Python class
    - [Creating the Todo Schema](/en/docs/fastapi/todo-api/creating-the-todo-schema): Pydantic schemas — the shape of data at the API boundary, separate from the database model
    - [Create Todo — Your First Endpoint](/en/docs/fastapi/todo-api/create-todo-endpoint): The FastAPI app, the database session dependency, and your first route
    - [Running & Testing Your API](/en/docs/fastapi/todo-api/running-and-testing): Starting uvicorn, and trying your endpoint through the interactive docs
    - [Fetch All Todos](/en/docs/fastapi/todo-api/fetch-all-todos): A GET endpoint that returns a list, and querying every row with SQLAlchemy
    - [Fetch a Single Todo](/en/docs/fastapi/todo-api/fetch-single-todo): Path parameters, filtering a query, and returning a proper 404
    - [Update Todo — PUT vs PATCH](/en/docs/fastapi/todo-api/update-todo): Replacing a todo entirely, updating it partially, and the real difference between the two
    - [Delete Todo](/en/docs/fastapi/todo-api/delete-todo): Removing a row, and returning a plain message instead of the resource

# Docs

- Python Notes
  - [Python Learning Notes (Tanglish)](/tanglish/docs): Phase vaara Python notes, JS/TS developer ku easy ah puriya maadhiri
  - Phase 1 — Core Foundations
    - [Phase 1 — Python Core Foundations](/tanglish/docs/phase-1): Indha phase oda goals, mattrum full JS/TS → Python cheat sheet
    - [Syntax & Indentation](/tanglish/docs/phase-1/syntax-and-indentation): JS/TS-la irundhu varra unakku Python oda periya rule — indentation than block-a define pannum
    - [Variables & Constants](/tanglish/docs/phase-1/variables-and-constants): const, let, var edhuvum kidayathu — Python-la straight ah assign pannalam
    - [Data Types & None](/tanglish/docs/phase-1/data-types-and-none): str, int, float, bool, None, mattrum type() vechi type check pannradhu
    - [Printing & String Interpolation](/tanglish/docs/phase-1/printing-and-strings): console.log() ku badhila print(), template literal ku badhila f-string
    - [Operators](/tanglish/docs/phase-1/operators): Arithmetic, comparison, logical operators — &&, ||, ! ku badhila and, or, not
    - [if / elif / else](/tanglish/docs/phase-1/conditionals): Conditionals, nested conditions sagitham
    - [for, range() & while](/tanglish/docs/phase-1/loops): Python-la loop pannradhu — JS/TS-la irundhu periya syntax change
    - [break, continue & pass](/tanglish/docs/phase-1/loop-control): Loops-a control pannradhu, mattrum "innum onnum implement pannala" keyword
  - Phase 2 — Collections
    - [Phase 2 — Collections](/tanglish/docs/phase-2): Indha phase oda goals, mattrum full JS/TS → Python cheat sheet
    - [list, Indexing & Slicing](/tanglish/docs/phase-2/lists): Python oda array — ordered, mutable, duplicates-um allow pannum
    - [append, remove & pop](/tanglish/docs/phase-2/list-methods): Nee constant-a use pannura moonu list methods
    - [tuple](/tanglish/docs/phase-2/tuples): Create pannina apparam change panna mudiyatha list
    - [set](/tanglish/docs/phase-2/sets): Automatic-a duplicates-a remove pannura collection
    - [dict](/tanglish/docs/phase-2/dictionaries): Python oda object — backend work ku probably most important type
    - [get, keys, values & items](/tanglish/docs/phase-2/dictionary-methods): dict-a safe-a read pannradhukku, loop pannradhukku use pannura methods
    - [Nested Data & in](/tanglish/docs/phase-2/nested-data-and-in): Dicts oda list (backend code-la romba common), mattrum Python oda membership operator
  - Phase 3 — Functions
    - [Phase 3 — Functions](/tanglish/docs/phase-3): Indha phase oda goals, mattrum full JS/TS → Python cheat sheet
    - [Defining Functions](/tanglish/docs/phase-3/functions-basics): function ku badhila def, parameters, mattrum return
    - [Type Hints](/tanglish/docs/phase-3/type-hints): TypeScript oda parameter mattrum return types oda Python equivalent
    - [Default & Keyword Arguments](/tanglish/docs/phase-3/default-and-keyword-arguments): Optional parameters, mattrum argument name vechi function call pannradhu
    - [*args & **kwargs](/tanglish/docs/phase-3/args-and-kwargs): Edhavadhu number of positional allathu keyword arguments-a accept pannradhu
  - Phase 4 — Python OOP
    - [Phase 4 — Python OOP](/tanglish/docs/phase-4): Indha phase oda goals, mattrum full TypeScript → Python cheat sheet
    - [class & object](/tanglish/docs/phase-4/classes-and-objects): Class define pannradhu, object create pannradhu — new keyword edhuvum illa
    - [__init__ & self](/tanglish/docs/phase-4/init-and-self): Python oda constructor, mattrum this-ku explicit stand-in
    - [Methods](/tanglish/docs/phase-4/methods): Class-kulla irukura functions — mattrum self yen innum varudhu
    - [Inheritance & super()](/tanglish/docs/phase-4/inheritance): extends parentheses aagum, super() almost same maadhiri work aagum
  - Phase 5 — Python-specific Features
    - [Phase 5 — Python-specific Features](/tanglish/docs/phase-5): Indha phase oda goals, mattrum full JS/TS → Python cheat sheet
    - [List Comprehension](/tanglish/docs/phase-5/list-comprehension): Oru list-a build pannradhukku one-line way — Python oda .map() mattrum .filter() version
    - [Dictionary Comprehension](/tanglish/docs/phase-5/dictionary-comprehension): List comprehension oda same idea than, aana dict build pannum
    - [enumerate](/tanglish/docs/phase-5/enumerate): List-a loop pannum bothu index-um serthu edukradhu
    - [zip](/tanglish/docs/phase-5/zip): Rendu lists-a onnaaga, pair by pair loop pannradhu
  - Phase 6 — Exceptions + Modules
    - [Phase 6 — Exceptions + Modules](/tanglish/docs/phase-6): Indha phase oda goals, mattrum full JS/TS → Python cheat sheet
    - [try / except](/tanglish/docs/phase-6/try-except): Python oda try/catch — aana specific error-a name pannanum-nu solum
    - [raise](/tanglish/docs/phase-6/raise): Python oda throw — generic Error ku badhila built-in exception types
    - [Modules & Imports](/tanglish/docs/phase-6/modules-and-imports): Python files eppadi pesikkum — export keyword edhuvum thevai illa
  - Phase 7 — Type Hints
    - [Phase 7 — Type Hints](/tanglish/docs/phase-7): Indha phase oda goals, mattrum full TypeScript → Python cheat sheet
    - [Variable & Function Hints](/tanglish/docs/phase-7/variable-and-function-hints): Plain values-a annotate pannradhu, mattrum function type hints recap
    - [Container Hints](/tanglish/docs/phase-7/container-hints): list allathu dict-kulla enna irukku-nu describe pannradhu, idhu oru list-nu matum illa
    - [Optional & Nested Types](/tanglish/docs/phase-7/optional-and-nested): None aaga vaaippu irukura value, mattrum container hints-a serthu combine pannradhu
  - Phase 8 — async / await
    - [Phase 8 — async / await](/tanglish/docs/phase-8): Indha phase oda goals, mattrum JS/TS → Python cheat sheet
    - [def, async def & await](/tanglish/docs/phase-8/async-and-await): JS async/await panra same idea than — keywords-um almost same than
  - [Final Practice — Build a User Store](/tanglish/docs/final-practice): Tutorial-a close pannitu idha nee build pannu — FastAPI ku best prep

  - [Backend Development with FastAPI](/tanglish/docs/fastapi): A syllabus for teaching backend development with FastAPI
  - Web Fundamentals
    - [What is the Internet?](/tanglish/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/what-is-the-internet): The network that makes backend development possible

    - [Putting It Together — How Does YouTube Work?](/tanglish/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/how-youtube-works): A real-world walkthrough that ties client, backend, database, and file storage together
  - Getting Started
    - [What is FastAPI?](/tanglish/docs/fastapi/getting-started/what-is-fastapi): A modern Python framework built for writing APIs fast, with less code

    - [Environment Configuration](/tanglish/docs/fastapi/getting-started/environment-configuration): Keeping database credentials out of your code with a .env file
    - [Database Connection](/tanglish/docs/fastapi/getting-started/database-connection): Turning your connection string into a real connection with SQLAlchemy
  - Building the Todo API
    - [Creating the Todo Model](/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/creating-the-todo-model): Describing a database table as a Python class
    - [Creating the Todo Schema](/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/creating-the-todo-schema): Pydantic schemas — the shape of data at the API boundary, separate from the database model
    - [Create Todo — Your First Endpoint](/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/create-todo-endpoint): The FastAPI app, the database session dependency, and your first route
    - [Running & Testing Your API](/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/running-and-testing): Starting uvicorn, and trying your endpoint through the interactive docs
    - [Fetch All Todos](/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/fetch-all-todos): A GET endpoint that returns a list, and querying every row with SQLAlchemy
